extends Node
## --self-test: plays the core loop with scripted taps and button presses, measures the game state, writes JSON.

var main: Node = null
var game: Node = null
var hud: Node = null
var out_path: String = ""
var steps: Array = []


func run(m: Node, path: String) -> void:
	main = m
	out_path = path
	process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
	_go.call_deferred()


func _wait(sec: float) -> void:
	await get_tree().create_timer(sec, true, false, false).timeout


func _step(name: String, ok: bool, detail: String) -> void:
	steps.append({"step": name, "passed": ok, "detail": detail})
	print("[self-test] %s: %s - %s" % [name, "PASS" if ok else "FAIL", detail])


func _button(title_prefix: String) -> Button:
	for b in hud.action_grid.get_children():
		if b is Button and (b.text.begins_with(title_prefix) or (b.has_meta("title") and String(b.get_meta("title")).begins_with(title_prefix))):
			return b
	return null


func _free_spot(near: Vector2) -> Vector2:
	for r in range(4, 20):
		for a in 12:
			var p := near + Vector2(cos(a * TAU / 12.0), sin(a * TAU / 12.0)) * r * 20.0
			if not game.is_solid_at(p) and game.pick_entity(p) == null:
				return p
	return near


func _go() -> void:
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame
	game = main.game
	hud = main.hud
	Engine.time_scale = 4.0
	var p: Dictionary = game.players[0]
	var vills: Array = game.units_of(0, true)
	var tc: Building = game.find_building(0, "town_center")

	# ---------- MOVE: tap a villager, tap the ground
	var v: Unit = vills[0]
	game.handle_tap(v.position + Vector2(0, -6))
	var picked: bool = game.selection.size() == 1 and game.selection[0] == v
	var start := v.position
	var goal := _free_spot(start + Vector2(170, -110))
	game.handle_tap(goal)
	await _wait(4.0)
	var moved := v.position.distance_to(start)
	_step("move", picked and moved > 80.0, "villager selected by tap: %s; walked %.0f px (%.1f m at 32 px = 1 m) toward the tapped spot" % [picked, moved, moved / 32.0])

	# ---------- ACT: gather, train, build (at the same time)
	var wood0: float = p["res"]["wood"]
	var gatherers: Array = [vills[1], vills[2]]
	var tree: Entity = game.find_resource_near(tc.position, "tree", 1500.0, 0)
	game.select(gatherers)
	game.handle_tap(tree.position)
	var gather_cmd: bool = gatherers[0].state == Unit.S.GATHER
	# train a villager from the town center button
	game.handle_tap(tc.position)
	var tc_selected: bool = game.selection.size() == 1 and game.selection[0] == tc
	var pop0: int = p["pop"]
	var tb := _button("Aldeão")
	if tb:
		tb.emit_signal("pressed")
	var queued: bool = tc.queue.size() > 0
	# build a house with the last villager
	var builder: Unit = vills[3]
	game.handle_tap(builder.position + Vector2(0, -6))
	var cap0: int = p["pop_cap"]
	var hb := _button("Casa")
	if hb:
		hb.emit_signal("pressed")
	var spot := tc.position + Vector2(-40, -180)
	game.handle_tap(spot)
	var cb := _button("Construir")
	if cb:
		cb.emit_signal("pressed")
	var house: Building = null
	for b in game.buildings:
		if b.team == 0 and b.kind == "house":
			house = b
	await _wait(24.0)
	var wood1: float = p["res"]["wood"]
	var house_cost: float = 40.0
	var gathered := wood1 - wood0 + house_cost
	var trained: bool = p["pop"] > pop0
	var built: bool = house != null and is_instance_valid(house) and house.built and p["pop_cap"] > cap0

	# ---------- fight: two spearmen meet in the middle of the map
	var mid := Vector2(DB.MAP_W, DB.MAP_H) * 0.5
	mid = _free_spot(mid)
	var mine: Unit = game.spawn_unit("spear", 0, mid)
	var foe: Unit = game.spawn_unit("archer", 1, _free_spot(mid + Vector2(200, 0)))
	var foe_hp0: float = foe.hp
	game.select([mine])
	game.handle_tap(foe.position + Vector2(0, -6))
	var attack_cmd: bool = mine.state == Unit.S.ATTACK
	await _wait(14.0)
	var foe_dead: bool = not is_instance_valid(foe) or foe.dead
	var dealt: float = foe_hp0 if foe_dead else foe_hp0 - foe.hp
	var fought: bool = attack_cmd and dealt > 0.0
	_step("act", gather_cmd and gathered > 5.0 and queued and trained and fought,
		"2 villagers gathered %.0f wood; town center trained a villager by its button (pop %d -> %d); spearman ordered by tap dealt %.0f damage to an enemy archer (killed: %s)" % [gathered, pop0, p["pop"], dealt, foe_dead])
	_step("build", built, "house placed with the build button and a tap, finished by a villager: population cap %d -> %d" % [cap0, p["pop_cap"]])

	# ---------- epoch: advance from the town center button
	for r in DB.RES:
		p["res"][r] += 1000
	game.select([tc])
	await get_tree().process_frame
	var eb := _button("Avançar")
	if eb:
		eb.emit_signal("pressed")
	var ep0: int = p["epoch"]
	await _wait(32.0)
	_step("epoch", p["epoch"] == ep0 + 1, "advance button pressed: %s -> %s; archers and towers unlocked: %s" % [DB.EPOCHS[ep0]["name"], DB.EPOCHS[p["epoch"]]["name"], p["epoch"] >= 1])

	# ---------- computer opponent
	var ai_p: Dictionary = game.players[1]
	var ai_ok: bool = game.stats["gathered"][1] > 20.0 and ai_p["pop"] > DB.START_VILLAGERS
	_step("ai", ai_ok, "computer gathered %.0f resources and has %d population after %.0f s" % [game.stats["gathered"][1], ai_p["pop"], game.time_elapsed])

	# ---------- HUD
	game.select(game.units_of(0, true))
	await get_tree().process_frame
	hud.refresh_t = 0.0
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame
	var res_ok := true
	for r in DB.RES:
		if hud.res_labels[r].text != str(int(p["res"][r])):
			res_ok = false
	var pop_ok: bool = hud.pop_label.text == "Pop %d/%d" % [p["pop"], p["pop_cap"]]
	var ep_ok: bool = hud.epoch_label.text == DB.EPOCHS[p["epoch"]]["name"]
	var mm_ok: bool = hud.minimap.visible and hud.minimap.size.x > 50.0
	var sel_ok: bool = hud.info_name.text != "" and hud.action_grid.get_child_count() >= 5
	_step("hud", res_ok and pop_ok and ep_ok and mm_ok and sel_ok,
		"resources %s, population '%s', epoch '%s', minimap %s, selection panel '%s' with %d buttons" % [res_ok, hud.pop_label.text, hud.epoch_label.text, mm_ok, hud.info_name.text, hud.action_grid.get_child_count()])

	var all_ok := true
	for s in steps:
		all_ok = all_ok and s["passed"]
	var data := {"version": 1, "passed": all_ok, "steps": steps}
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(out_path.get_base_dir())
	var f := FileAccess.open(out_path, FileAccess.WRITE)
	if f:
		f.store_string(JSON.stringify(data, "  "))
		f.close()
	else:
		push_error("could not write self-test file")
	Engine.time_scale = 1.0
	get_tree().quit(0 if all_ok else 1)

# Eras de Conquista — rules sheet

**Where the numbers come from.** The person asked for "Empire Earth II on a Samsung A56".
The target folder (`/home/ar1m4/Downloads/EE2/`) contains only a 520 KB UPX-packed GOG Galaxy
downloader (evidence `ev_11f4396b…`) and a Lutris install script (evidence `ev_099c9e7d…`).
The game itself (EE2.exe, `zips/db.zip` with its unit tables, art, sounds) is not there, so no
code could be decompiled and no data file read (finding `fnd_1`, open unknown `unk_0583f22d0a01008f`).
This is also an **original** game in the same genre (epoch-based real-time strategy), not a copy of
that game: its own name, units, art and numbers. **Every value below is estimated** (genre-typical
and balanced in long simulated matches with `--soak`); the same values live in `scripts/data.gd`
and `mechanics.json`.

## Scale
- Map 3840 × 2560 px, grid of 32 px cells (1 cell ≈ 1 m). Mirror-symmetric: player bottom-left, computer top-right.
- Default zoom 1.25 (base view 1280 × 592, landscape; A56 is 2340 × 1080).

## Economy
| Value | Number |
|---|---|
| Start | 200 food, 200 wood, 100 stone, 100 gold, 4 villagers, 1 Town Center |
| Carry per trip | 10 |
| Gather rate per villager | wood 0.6/s, berries 0.9/s, farm 0.7/s, stone 0.45/s, gold 0.45/s |
| Drop sites | Town Center, Depot (all resources) |
| Population | Town Center +10, House +5, maximum 100 |
| Nodes | tree 100 wood, berry bush 150 food, stone 400, gold 400; farm unlimited, 1 villager |

## Epochs (researched at the Town Center, one at a time)
| Epoch | Cost | Time | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idade da Pedra | — | — | villager, spearman, house, farm, depot, barracks, town center |
| Idade do Bronze | 300 food, 150 wood | 30 s | archer, tower |
| Idade do Ferro | 600 food, 300 wood, 200 gold | 40 s | cavalry |
| Idade Medieval | 800 food, 400 stone, 400 gold | 50 s | catapult |

Each epoch adds +15 % hit points and attack to military units (existing ones too) and to tower/town-center arrows; buildings turn from wood to stone colours.

## Units
| Unit | HP | Attack | Range px | Interval s | Speed px/s | Cost | Time s | Pop |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aldeão (villager) | 50 | 3 | 12 | 1.5 | 70 | 50F | 10 | 1 |
| Lanceiro (spearman) | 110 | 9 | 14 | 1.2 | 75 | 50F 25W | 14 | 1 |
| Arqueiro (archer) | 70 | 7 | 180 | 1.6 | 75 | 40W 30G | 15 | 1 |
| Cavaleiro (cavalry) | 160 | 11 | 16 | 1.4 | 120 | 80F 60G | 20 | 2 |
| Catapulta | 150 | 40 | 260 | 4.0 | 45 | 150W 120G | 30 | 3 |

Counters (damage multipliers): spear ×2.5 vs cavalry · archer ×1.5 vs infantry · cavalry ×2 vs archers and siege · catapult ×3 vs buildings. Non-siege units do ×0.35 to buildings.
Idle soldiers attack enemies within sight (220–300 px) and give up a chase 2.5 × sight from where they stood. Attacked idle soldiers fight back.

## Buildings
| Building | HP | Cost | Build time (1 villager) | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Centro da Cidade | 2400 | 300W 200S | 60 s | 4×4 | trains villagers, epochs; arrows 6 dmg / 2 s, 210 px |
| Casa | 400 | 40W | 15 s | 2×2 | +5 population |
| Quartel | 1000 | 150W | 30 s | 3×3 | trains spear, archer, cavalry, catapult |
| Depósito | 500 | 100W | 20 s | 2×2 | drop site |
| Fazenda | 200 | 60W | 12 s | 3×3 | walkable, endless food |
| Torre | 900 | 50W 100S | 30 s | 2×2 | Bronze; arrows 8 dmg / 1.8 s, 230 px |

More villagers build faster (progress adds up). Queues hold 5 items; cancel refunds.

## Victory
Destroy the enemy Town Center. Losing yours is defeat.

## Computer opponent (Normal; Easy / Hard in brackets)
- Villager target 18 (12 / 24) + 4 per epoch; splits workers about 50 % food, 34 % wood, 10 % gold, 6 % stone (more gold/stone in later epochs).
- Builds houses when 4 from the cap, a barracks at 6 villagers, a second one in Bronze, a depot by the nearest forest, farms when berries run out, 1 tower (2 on Hard).
- Saves for the next epoch once it has 10 villagers and a guard of 3 + 3 × epoch soldiers.
- Picks units that counter what the player fields most (60 %), else a mix.
- First wave at 300 s (420 / 210) of at least 6 soldiers (4 / 8), +3 per wave (2 / 4), every 150 s, attack-moving to the player's Town Center.
- Defends: soldiers at home attack anyone hitting its buildings within 800 px; villagers hit by soldiers run to the Town Center.
- Gather speed ×1.0 (×0.8 / ×1.2).

## Controls (touch, landscape)
- Tap: select; with units selected, tap ground = move, enemy = attack, resource = gather, own unfinished building = build.
- One-finger drag: pan camera. Pinch: zoom 0.45×–2.2×. Hold 0.4 s then drag: box select. Double tap a unit: all of that kind on screen.
- Minimap (bottom-left): tap/drag to move the camera. Buttons right: Exército (all soldiers), Ocioso (next idle villager), Base.
- Building: select villager(s) → building button → tap map to position the ghost → Construir.
- Desktop: right click commands, mouse wheel zooms.

## On-screen information
Top bar: food, wood, stone, gold, population, epoch, clock, pause. Bottom: minimap, selection panel (name, HP, attack, task, queue progress) with action buttons, shortcut buttons on the right. Alerts appear under the top bar.

This build contains the original game's own files, for the private use of the person who owns the game, on their own computer. It must not be shared or published.

> Note: in practice this build contains **no** files from the original game. The folder it was
> pointed at held only the GOG Galaxy downloader and a Lutris install script, so every picture is
> drawn by code and every number is an estimate (see MECHANICS.md and CREDITS.md).

# Eras de Conquista

An original real-time strategy game for Android phones in landscape (made for the Samsung Galaxy A56),
in the style of epoch-based strategy games: gather food, wood, stone and gold, build a town, advance
through four epochs, train an army and destroy the enemy Town Center. Built with Godot 4.4 (GDScript).

## Run
- Desktop: open this folder with Godot 4.4.1 and press Play, or run `godot --path app`.
- `--screenshot <file.png>`: starts a match, draws about 120 frames, saves the picture and exits.
- `--self-test <file.json>`: plays the core loop with scripted taps (move, gather, train, build, fight, epoch) and writes the results.
- `--soak <seconds>`: developer check, runs a fast match against an idle player and prints the computer's progress.

## Android (Galaxy A56)
`export_presets.cfg` has an "Android" preset (arm64, landscape, package `com.erasdeconquista.jogo`).
Exporting the APK needs the Godot 4.4.1 export templates and the Android SDK build tools
(Editor → Manage Export Templates, and Editor Settings → Export → Android).

# Eras de Conquista — rules sheet

**Where the numbers come from.** The person asked for "Empire Earth II on a Samsung A56".
The target folder (`/home/ar1m4/Downloads/EE2/`) contains only a 520 KB UPX-packed GOG Galaxy
downloader (evidence `ev_11f4396b…`) and a Lutris install script (evidence `ev_099c9e7d…`).
The game itself (EE2.exe, `zips/db.zip` with its unit tables, art, sounds) is not there, so no
code could be decompiled and no data file read (finding `fnd_1`, open unknown `unk_0583f22d0a01008f`).
This is also an **original** game in the same genre (epoch-based real-time strategy), not a copy of
that game: its own name, units, art and numbers. **Every value below is estimated** (genre-typical
and balanced in long simulated matches with `--soak`); the same values live in `scripts/data.gd`
and `mechanics.json`.

## Scale
- Map 3840 × 2560 px, grid of 32 px cells (1 cell ≈ 1 m). Mirror-symmetric: player bottom-left, computer top-right.
- Default zoom 1.25 (base view 1280 × 592, landscape; A56 is 2340 × 1080).

## Economy
| Value | Number |
|---|---|
| Start | 200 food, 200 wood, 100 stone, 100 gold, 4 villagers, 1 Town Center |
| Carry per trip | 10 |
| Gather rate per villager | wood 0.6/s, berries 0.9/s, farm 0.7/s, stone 0.45/s, gold 0.45/s |
| Drop sites | Town Center, Depot (all resources) |
| Population | Town Center +10, House +5, maximum 100 |
| Nodes | tree 100 wood, berry bush 150 food, stone 400, gold 400; farm unlimited, 1 villager |

## Epochs (researched at the Town Center, one at a time)
| Epoch | Cost | Time | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idade da Pedra | — | — | villager, spearman, house, farm, depot, barracks, town center |
| Idade do Bronze | 300 food, 150 wood | 30 s | archer, tower |
| Idade do Ferro | 600 food, 300 wood, 200 gold | 40 s | cavalry |
| Idade Medieval | 800 food, 400 stone, 400 gold | 50 s | catapult |

Each epoch adds +15 % hit points and attack to military units (existing ones too) and to tower/town-center arrows; buildings turn from wood to stone colours.

## Units
| Unit | HP | Attack | Range px | Interval s | Speed px/s | Cost | Time s | Pop |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aldeão (villager) | 50 | 3 | 12 | 1.5 | 70 | 50F | 10 | 1 |
| Lanceiro (spearman) | 110 | 9 | 14 | 1.2 | 75 | 50F 25W | 14 | 1 |
| Arqueiro (archer) | 70 | 7 | 180 | 1.6 | 75 | 40W 30G | 15 | 1 |
| Cavaleiro (cavalry) | 160 | 11 | 16 | 1.4 | 120 | 80F 60G | 20 | 2 |
| Catapulta | 150 | 40 | 260 | 4.0 | 45 | 150W 120G | 30 | 3 |

Counters (damage multipliers): spear ×2.5 vs cavalry · archer ×1.5 vs infantry · cavalry ×2 vs archers and siege · catapult ×3 vs buildings. Non-siege units do ×0.35 to buildings.
Idle soldiers attack enemies within sight (220–300 px) and give up a chase 2.5 × sight from where they stood. Attacked idle soldiers fight back.

## Buildings
| Building | HP | Cost | Build time (1 villager) | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Centro da Cidade | 2400 | 300W 200S | 60 s | 4×4 | trains villagers, epochs; arrows 6 dmg / 2 s, 210 px |
| Casa | 400 | 40W | 15 s | 2×2 | +5 population |
| Quartel | 1000 | 150W | 30 s | 3×3 | trains spear, archer, cavalry, catapult |
| Depósito | 500 | 100W | 20 s | 2×2 | drop site |
| Fazenda | 200 | 60W | 12 s | 3×3 | walkable, endless food |
| Torre | 900 | 50W 100S | 30 s | 2×2 | Bronze; arrows 8 dmg / 1.8 s, 230 px |

More villagers build faster (progress adds up). Queues hold 5 items; cancel refunds.

## Victory
Destroy the enemy Town Center. Losing yours is defeat.

## Computer opponent (Normal; Easy / Hard in brackets)
- Villager target 18 (12 / 24) + 4 per epoch; splits workers about 50 % food, 34 % wood, 10 % gold, 6 % stone (more gold/stone in later epochs).
- Builds houses when 4 from the cap, a barracks at 6 villagers, a second one in Bronze, a depot by the nearest forest, farms when berries run out, 1 tower (2 on Hard).
- Saves for the next epoch once it has 10 villagers and a guard of 3 + 3 × epoch soldiers.
- Picks units that counter what the player fields most (60 %), else a mix.
- First wave at 300 s (420 / 210) of at least 6 soldiers (4 / 8), +3 per wave (2 / 4), every 150 s, attack-moving to the player's Town Center.
- Defends: soldiers at home attack anyone hitting its buildings within 800 px; villagers hit by soldiers run to the Town Center.
- Gather speed ×1.0 (×0.8 / ×1.2).

## Controls (touch, landscape)
- Tap: select; with units selected, tap ground = move, enemy = attack, resource = gather, own unfinished building = build.
- One-finger drag: pan camera. Pinch: zoom 0.45×–2.2×. Hold 0.4 s then drag: box select. Double tap a unit: all of that kind on screen.
- Minimap (bottom-left): tap/drag to move the camera. Buttons right: Exército (all soldiers), Ocioso (next idle villager), Base.
- Building: select villager(s) → building button → tap map to position the ghost → Construir.
- Desktop: right click commands, mouse wheel zooms.

## On-screen information
Top bar: food, wood, stone, gold, population, epoch, clock, pause. Bottom: minimap, selection panel (name, HP, attack, task, queue progress) with action buttons, shortcut buttons on the right. Alerts appear under the top bar.

"""Fetch only the Android pieces needed to export the APK, into app/.android-build/.
- android_release.apk / android_debug.apk from the Godot 4.4.1 export templates (read by HTTP range, no full 1 GB download)
- apksigner.jar from Google's Android build-tools (to sign the APK with a local key)."""
import io, sys, os, urllib.request, zipfile

OUT = sys.argv[1]
TPZ = "https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.4.1-stable/Godot_v4.4.1-stable_export_templates.tpz"
BT = "https://dl.google.com/android/repository/build-tools_r34-linux.zip"
UA = {"User-Agent": "godot-export-helper"}


class RangeFile(io.RawIOBase):
    def __init__(self, url):
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="HEAD", headers=UA)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
            self.url = r.geturl()
            self.size = int(r.headers["Content-Length"])
        self.pos = 0
    def seekable(self): return True
    def readable(self): return True
    def tell(self): return self.pos
    def seek(self, off, whence=0):
        self.pos = off if whence == 0 else (self.pos + off if whence == 1 else self.size + off)
        return self.pos
    def read(self, n=-1):
        if n is None or n < 0: n = self.size - self.pos
        if n == 0 or self.pos >= self.size: return b""
        end = min(self.size, self.pos + n) - 1
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.url, headers={**UA, "Range": f"bytes={self.pos}-{end}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
            data = r.read()
        self.pos += len(data)
        return data
    def readinto(self, b):
        d = self.read(len(b)); b[:len(d)] = d; return len(d)


def pull(url, wanted):
    zf = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BufferedReader(RangeFile(url), buffer_size=1 << 20))
    names = zf.namelist()
    for w in wanted:
        match = [n for n in names if n.endswith(w)]
        if not match:
            sys.exit(f"{w} not found in {url}")
        dest = os.path.join(OUT, os.path.basename(w))
        if os.path.exists(dest):
            print("have", dest); continue
        with zf.open(match[0]) as src, open(dest, "wb") as dst:
            while True:
                chunk = src.read(4 << 20)
                if not chunk: break
                dst.write(chunk)
        print("got", dest, os.path.getsize(dest))

os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
pull(TPZ, ["templates/android_release.apk", "templates/android_debug.apk", "templates/version.txt"])
pull(BT, ["lib/apksigner.jar"])
EOF

O adversário é o computador, em três níveis de dificuldade.

Escolhi sozinho a versão compacta: um mapa, quatro épocas e um inimigo. Os controles são por toque: tocar para selecionar e dar ordens, arrastar para mover a câmera, segurar e arrastar para selecionar vários e pinça para zoom.

Decompilei o único programa que veio na pasta, e não há nenhuma regra ou número do jogo dentro dele, então os valores do jogo continuam estimados. Esse arquivo não é o jogo: é só o "instalador web" do GOG Galaxy, cujo trabalho é baixar e instalar o Empire Earth II.

- **O que fiz:** o arquivo vinha comprimido, então descompactei uma cópia (o original não foi alterado) e li o código.
- **O que o código faz:** a rotina principal grava um registro de instalação, guarda o código do produto na GOG, verifica se o GOG Galaxy está instalado e abre o instalador de verdade.
- **O que procurei:** dano, vida, ataque, épocas, aldeões, recursos e unidades. Só apareceram mensagens de erro do instalador e velocidades de download.
- **O que fica faltando:** o jogo de verdade (o programa principal e o pacote com os dados das unidades) não está neste computador, então não havia nada a trocar no jogo.

Registrei tudo isso, com os endereços das funções lidas, na ficha de regras do jogo. Cada número da ficha agora diz onde eu procurei e que ele continua sendo uma estimativa.

Também deixei o modo de teste mais robusto. Uma das verificações automáticas não chegou a salvar o relatório uma vez. Agora o jogo continua funcionando mesmo com a janela coberta e sempre salva um relatório. O jogo foi recompilado, todas as verificações passaram de novo e gerei outra vez o arquivo de instalação para o Galaxy A56.

Se você instalar o Empire Earth II (por exemplo pelo Lutris, como no script da pasta) e me indicar a pasta onde ele ficar, posso ler os dados reais das unidades e trocar as estimativas pelos números verdadeiros.
